pr_title: Don't raise when setting HVAC mode without a mode ZwaveValue
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When we can't get a ZwaveValue for the mode attribute of a zwave_js thermostat, we set the available HVAC modes to `heat`. If a scene is used to capture the state of such a thermostat and reapply it, it attempts to set the HVAC mode to `heat`. This currently raises an exception, so this change makes it a no-op

review_comments:
I think the existing and new solutions are both incorrect.
Just because a device doesn't show an HVAC mode currently, doesn't mean it is not supported. It could be unavailable or unknown at this time as well (just `None`).

I would suggest on checking it against the actual exposed `hvac_modes` instead.

`self._current_mode` isn't the actual state of the current HVAC mode, it's the ZwaveValue stored in the zwave_js driver that contains, among other things, both the available HVAC modes (`states` key) and the current HVAC mode (`value` key), like so:
```
{
      "commandClassName": "Thermostat Mode",
      "commandClass": 64,
      "endpoint": 1,
      "property": "mode",
      "propertyName": "mode",
      "metadata": {
        "type": "number",
        "readable": true,
        "writeable": true,
        "min": 0,
        "max": 31,
        "label": "Thermostat mode",
        "states": { "0": "Off", "1": "Heat", "2": "Cool", "3": "Auto" }
      },
      "value": 1
    }
```
If it is `None`, it means that we weren't able to find that ZwaveValue on the device, and we therefore have no way to send a new mode to the device, either because the device doesn't support setting a mode (like in the linked issue) or because the device was not properly interviewed. Because we look for the ZwaveValue on initialization of the entity, I am not sure that this would be correctable by the entity even if the ZwaveValue somehow became available on the driver later.

Does that make sense? And if so, do you still feel that this is an incorrect approach?
Maybe we need to rename that variable since as I was writing the above, I realized it captures both the current mode and available modes

I spoke to kpine on Discord and he interpreted your comment differently. While I am not sure if it addresses your concern, what he proposed does make more sense so I have updated the logic accordingly

> self._current_mode isn't the actual state of the current HVAC mode, it's the ZwaveValue stored in the zwave_js driver that contains

That was my confusion spot on. So my comment is invalid. Thanks for pointing that out 👍
